account:
Today has mostly followed municipal routine: the morning mill inspection, office business, and now my arrival at the neighbour's dockside cottage for three o'clock tea. The mill stall held two stacks of sixty-four hay bales when I checked; I saw none removed. The builder submitted a limited visual bridge report saying the accessible crossing was passable, without certifying structural safety. The secretary confirms the agreed two-emerald fee was paid at 07:58, so that obligation is settled.

The unusual matter is repeated, extremely vague talk of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk 11 and 02 repeated it, and the neighbour has heard similar talk. Neither the secretary nor I has established a specific change or found an eyewitness explanation. I did not find the baker in the visible bakery interior earlier; he was later seen at the market stall. His absence alone proves nothing. I still want his firsthand account. I cannot yet say what the supposed change is for, or whether anything actually happened.

Office communication has also been confused. I borrowed and returned all five records, but the secretary subsequently described the chest as empty and asked whether I still had them. My inventory is empty of books after returning them. This may simply be an outdated observation, not evidence of wrongdoing. No new council correspondence was identified during my review. I asked the secretary to retain correspondence for my 16:30 return and record any specific firsthand bakery evidence. I heard the builder speaking and shouting during my walk here, but could not make out his words, so I cannot infer their subject. Tea offers a chance to hear whether the neighbour has learned anything concrete, while keeping my appointment.
